A.reason: Krupp et al. 2012 is ref 55, cited once in the Discussion as one of the 'previous studies conducted in children' with which the hippuric acid–fruit/vegetable association is 'consistent'. The paper's replication tests its own IDEFICS/I.Family discovery findings in the DONALD cohort, not Krupp's finding.

notes: Within-paper replication only (codebook negative genre). Metabolites are discovered in IDEFICS/I.Family and then 'replicated' in the independent DONALD cohort within the same paper; the Introduction frames DONALD as a check on 'the reproducibility of findings'. Previously published biomarker findings (hippuric acid [16,55,56], proline betaine [73], phloretin [74]) are compared only after the fact ('consistent with', 'could not be replicated in our study') and are not the target of a designed replication. Ambiguity: the abstract says it assesses 'the replicability of previously reported biomarkers', and DONALD is the same cohort Krupp 2012 used. A second coder could therefore code a conceptual replication of Krupp 2012's hippuric acid finding (success). The body text does not support that reading.
